Follow-Up Care Guidelines for Orthopedic Surgery Patients

Proper follow-up care is essential for a successful recovery after orthopedic surgery. This document outlines the standard schedule and expectations for post-operative follow-up visits and home care activities.

Post-Operative Visit Schedule:
The typical follow-up schedule after a total knee replacement includes visits at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year post-surgery. Your surgeon may adjust this schedule based on your individual recovery progress. It is critical that you attend all scheduled appointments even if you feel you are recovering well.

2-Week Post-Operative Visit:
At your two-week visit, your surgeon will inspect the incision site, remove staples or sutures if applicable, and evaluate for any signs of early infection or complications. Bring a list of all current medications. This visit will also include a review of your activity progress and any adjustments to your physical therapy program.

6-Week Post-Operative Visit:
By six weeks, most patients have improved significantly in mobility. Your surgeon will assess range of motion, evaluate gait, and review X-rays of the joint replacement. Physical therapy progress will be discussed. You may receive clearance to resume driving at this visit if your surgical leg is not the dominant driving leg and you have adequate pain control and strength.

3-Month Visit:
At three months, patients typically transition from formal physical therapy to a home exercise program. Your surgeon will assess functional outcomes and overall satisfaction. Any persistent pain, swelling, or stiffness should be reported and evaluated.

6-Month and 1-Year Visits:
These visits confirm long-term implant stability, track functional improvements, and detect any late complications. X-rays are typically taken at each of these visits to evaluate implant positioning.

Home Care Activities Between Visits:
Between visits, continue your home exercise program as prescribed. Monitor your incision and report any changes to your surgeon's office. Keep a log of your pain levels, swelling, and range of motion to share with your care team. Maintain a healthy diet and stay hydrated to support tissue healing.

When to Contact Your Care Team Before Scheduled Visits:
Contact your surgeon's office promptly if you experience: increased pain or swelling that is not improving, fever above 101°F, new or worsening drainage from the incision, difficulty achieving range of motion milestones set by your therapist, or any fall or trauma to the operative leg.

Medications During Recovery:
Do not start or stop any medications without consulting your surgeon or primary care physician. This includes over-the-counter medications and supplements. Blood thinners, antibiotics, and pain medications must be managed according to your prescription instructions throughout the recovery period.

Activity Restrictions During Follow-Up Period:
Avoid high-impact activities (running, jumping, heavy lifting) until cleared by your surgeon. Low-impact activities such as walking, swimming, and cycling are generally encouraged to maintain conditioning and joint health. Do not return to work or driving before receiving clearance from your surgical team.

Patient Education:
Use the resources provided by your care team, including physical therapy handouts and this discharge packet. Contact your care navigator or case manager if you have questions between appointments. Telemedicine visits may be available for non-urgent follow-up questions.
